meta.title: Help & guide – OpenFireMap
meta.description: How OpenFireMap works: the map on desktop and smartphone, export, town plan, overlay, and how to add fire hydrants to OpenStreetMap.
hero.title: Find fire water.
hero.lead: OpenFireMap shows fire hydrants, water supply points, fire stations and defibrillators from OpenStreetMap. Learn how the map works, how to print plans and how to add missing hydrants yourself.
hero.fact_coverage: Worldwide, extra fast in 45 European countries
steps.title: Three steps to the nearest hydrant
steps.label: Step
steps.s1_text: Type a place or address into the search field and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Or use the location button to find yourself.
steps.s2_text: Fire stations show up early. Hydrants and defibrillators appear from zoom level 15, with symbols from 17.
steps.s3_text: From zoom level 18, a symbol shows type, diameter, number and more as soon as you point at it with the mouse. Clicking or tapping a hydrant draws a 100 metre radius.
zoom.title: What you see at each zoom level
zoom.hint: The current zoom level is shown in the status box.
ui_tour.title: Every button explained
ui_tour.lead: Choose your device and click an entry. On a computer the tools sit at the top left; on a smartphone they are in the menu.
ui_tour.desktop_alt: OpenFireMap on a computer: map of Nuremberg's old town with hydrant symbols, search field and tool buttons at the top left, status box at the bottom right.
ui_tour.phone_alt: OpenFireMap on a smartphone with the menu open: map layers, share map view, search, map symbols, info & legal and local cache.
ui_tour.d_search_text: Enter a place, street or address. The map jumps there.
ui_tour.d_locate_text: Shows where you are. Your browser asks for permission once.
ui_tour.d_layers_text: Choose a background: standard, print, night, satellite, topographic, OSM and BayernAtlas.
ui_tour.d_export_text: Hydrant plan as PNG or PDF, points as GPX or CSV.
ui_tour.d_share_text: Copies a link to exactly this map view.
ui_tour.d_marker_text: The letter shows the type, for example U for underground and O for pillar. The map symbols page explains every symbol.
ui_tour.d_status_text: Zoom level and data date. “Data status details” shows the source and age of the data.
ui_tour.d_legal_text: This help, map symbols, overlay, legal notice, privacy and licences.
ui_tour.m_menu_text: Opens all tools. Tap next to it to close it again.
ui_tour.m_status_text: Zoom level and data date. Tap it to see the source and age of the data.
ui_tour.m_layers_text: Change the background, for example to satellite for orientation.
ui_tour.m_share_text: A link to this view, for example for your group chat.
ui_tour.m_legal_text: This is also where you find this help.
ui_tour.m_note: Export and the town plan are only available on a computer. On a smartphone you can start OpenFireMap like an app via “Add to Home Screen”.

plan.title: From map view to printed plan
plan.lead: The town plan turns OpenFireMap into a print-ready sheet with grid, legend, north arrow, scale bar and street index. For the fire station wall, training or the folder in the vehicle.
plan.s1_text: Drag a frame on the map, choose paper size and scale.
plan.s2_text: Decide which objects, which legend and which index go on the sheet.
plan.s3_text: Place title, legend and index, then save as PDF or PNG.
contrib.title: A hydrant is missing? Add it.
contrib.lead: All data comes from OpenStreetMap. What you add there shows up in OpenFireMap once the services it relies on have processed the change. Pick the tool that suits you.
contrib.hj_text: Stand in front of the hydrant, take a photo, choose the type, upload. In under 20 seconds.
contrib.sc_text: Answer questions about objects nearby. Good for adding details on a walk.
contrib.id_text: Right on openstreetmap.org. Place a point, choose the “Fire Hydrant” preset, save.
contrib.josm_text: For many hydrants at once or careful work across a whole town.
contrib.rule_seen: Only add what you have seen on site yourself.
contrib.rule_copyright: Do not copy data from water utility plans without their permission.
contrib.rule_comment: When saving, add a short note on what you changed.
good.title: What OpenFireMap is and what it is not
good.alarm_title: In an emergency, always call first
good.alarm_text: OpenFireMap is not an operational resource. The data may be incomplete or out of date and does not replace information from dispatch centres or water utilities. In Europe the emergency number is 112.
good.osm_text: Volunteers add hydrants, stations and defibrillators. The more people contribute, the more complete the map becomes.
good.fresh_text: For Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg, OpenFireMap usually rebuilds the prepared data daily, for 40 more countries weekly. The map also requests new entries live.
good.free_text: A non-commercial project. The map runs in your browser.
good.keys_text: All menus, symbols and the export can be used without a mouse.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.contact_text: Write to us, we are happy to help.
faq.q1: Why don't I see any hydrants?
faq.a1: Hydrants appear from zoom level 15. Zoom in further. If you still see none, nobody has added any in this area yet. You can change that.
faq.q2: When will my new hydrant appear?
faq.a2: This cannot be predicted exactly. OpenFireMap requests new and changed objects through the Overpass API. They appear once the Overpass server has processed the change; caches can delay this a little. If Overpass is overloaded or unreachable, the change appears later. Deleted objects only disappear with the next data update. More under Data & freshness.
faq.q3: Why is there no export on a smartphone?
faq.a3: Print-ready plans need a lot of memory and a large screen for selecting the area. Export and the town plan are therefore only available on a computer.
faq.q4: May I print plans for my fire brigade?
faq.a4: Yes. The data is licensed under the Open Database License. Every plan must show “© OpenStreetMap contributors”. The town plan prints this credit automatically.
faq.a5: Only partly. Areas you have loaded stay in memory for a while. New areas and search need a connection. A printed town plan is more reliable on the road.
faq.q6: Is this an official fire service map?
faq.a6: No. OpenFireMap is a private, non-commercial project based on OpenStreetMap. It does not officially work with any authority or fire service.
faq.q7: How do I get the fire service layers into my own map?
faq.a7: With the overlay. The overlay page has a demo and a PDF guide. To get your domain enabled, drop us a line.
